clue.text: Provided backs in best tailored suits

indicators.note: in tells us the turned piece sits inside the rearranged letters
tailored suggests something cut and reshaped, so the letters of best are rearranged
backs tells us the word for provided is turned round to run the other way

parts.note: provided, as a conjunction, means if

explanation.surface: A conditional remark about the finest made-to-measure suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' rearranges the letters of best, 'backs' turns the conditional word round, and 'in' places it within. 'suits' looks like clothing but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit something is to be fitting for it, the same verb sense as suits in 'that colour suits you'.

clue.text: No 10 possibly concealed ring's oriental code

parts.note: a number 10 could be a bus route, rather than Downing Street
concealed means hid
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Downing Street has hidden a mysterious Eastern code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 10' suggests the Prime Minister's residence but is a bus number.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai code of honour in feudal Japan, an Eastern code of conduct.

clue.text: Hob quite left out

indicators.note: out tells us the abbreviation for left is removed

parts.note: quite, meaning moderately, is fairly

explanation.surface: A kitchen hob has been completely forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hob' looks like a cooker but is a hobgoblin, a mischievous sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: A hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous household sprite from folklore, one kind of elf.

clue.text: Vessel overturned by bow crest

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue turns the pot upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
a bow is a knot tied with loops

explanation.surface: A ship capsized by its bow at the top of a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses POT to TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft or crest of hair or feathers on top of the head.

clue.text: At intervals is put out in the form of a poem

definitions.text: in the form of a poem

indicators.note: put out tells us the word is is ejected from the longer word

parts.note: something occurring at intervals is episodic, happening in separate episodes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem whose occasional lines are thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes IS from EPISODIC, leaving EPODIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An epode is a lyric verse form, so the related adjective describes writing shaped like that kind of poem.

clue.text: A royal auditor's reproductions

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so auditor's points to what the ear hears

parts.note: prints are reproductions of pictures

explanation.surface: A royal accountant's copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a male member of a royal family, so he is a royal.

clue.text: Extract from a tree fruit revived graduates

indicators.note: revived suggests being brought back to life in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Students celebrating with fruit after their degrees, then refreshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Date sugar is a sweetener produced from dried dates, the fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Drinks containing nitrogen remains after blaze

indicators.note: containing tells us the drinks hold the chemical symbol inside

parts.note: ciders are drinks
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Drinks with added nitrogen are what's left after the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinders are the burnt residue of coal or wood left once a fire dies down.

clue.text: Mobile 3G unifier (ugh!) materially close to a body

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: 3G read as three Gs
taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A grumble about a 3G mobile phone that unites everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: '3G' reads as GGG; 'Mobile' rearranges GGG + UNIFIER + UGH. 'Mobile' looks like a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Figure-hugging clothes fit tightly, so the material clings close to the wearer's shape.

clue.text: Saxon standard square inches have their origins in a designated area

indicators.note: the origins of the four words are their initial letters, which we take in turn

explanation.surface: Old Saxon units of measurement trace back to a protected district.
explanation.walkthrough: SSSI stands for Site of Special Scientific Interest, a British conservation designation for land protected for its wildlife or geology.
explanation.definitionFit: A Site of Special Scientific Interest is land officially designated for protection in the UK, so it is a designated area.

clue.text: Curling his lip, Spike is uncultured

indicators.note: curling the words his lip twists them, signalling their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange
a tine is a prong or spike, as on a fork or antler

explanation.surface: Someone sneering with a curled lip while a man called Spike is a boor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curling' looks like the sport or a sneer, but it signals rearranging the letters of 'his lip'; 'Spike' is not a name but a prong.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine is a person hostile to art and learning, so used as an adjective it means lacking culture.

clue.text: It's representative of Chinese brooch, one in Scotland

parts.note: a brooch is a decorative pin
yin is the Scots dialect word for one

explanation.surface: A Chinese brooch and a single item somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots dialect 'yin' means one, as in 'the wee yin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinyin is the standard romanised spelling system that represents Mandarin sounds in Latin letters.

clue.text: Sundae with hot and cold shakes, not made liquid

indicators.note: shakes signals that the letters are jumbled about, like a milkshake

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An ice-cream sundae served with hot and cold milkshakes that never melted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shakes' rearranges SUNDAE plus H and C. 'liquid' is the finance sense: a cheque not cashed has not been turned into liquid money.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid assets are cash; a cheque left uncashed has not been converted into that ready money.

clue.text: She has a responsibility for a minor work method around river

definitions.text: She has a responsibility for a minor

parts.note: to work, as a machine does, is to go

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of method are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A woman responsible for a child uses a working method near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals rearranging the letters of 'method'. 'minor' means a child, not a small thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A godmother is a sponsor at a baptism who takes on spiritual responsibility for a child.

clue.text: Disease-ridden central Himalaya initially reneged on debts

indicators.note: central picks out the letters in the core of the mountain range's name
initially takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A diseased region in the mid-Himalayas defaulted on loans.
explanation.walkthrough: The four central letters of HIMALAYA give MALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarious means infested with malaria, so a malarious region is disease-ridden.

clue.text: Many years can be over, say, in a second

indicators.note: in tells us the flipped piece goes inside the other letters
over tells us the abbreviation is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: say, introducing an example, is abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time can pass in a single second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' flips the abbreviation for say, and 'in' places it within A and S; 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal word for a very long time, as in 'I waited for ages'.

clue.text: Unfair utterance by caveman put heartlessly

parts.note: ug is the grunt cartoon cavemen traditionally make

indicators.note: heartlessly tells us the middle letter of the word for put is removed

parts.note: to put something down is to lay it

explanation.surface: A caveman says something unjust, delivered without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the central A from LAY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair in the old sense of not fair-looking, plain or unattractive, matches a synonym for unsightly.

clue.text: Not a person in Cancun? Hum anthem!

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a Mexican resort, someone hums an anthem while unrecognisable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhuman means not human, the state of not being a person.

clue.text: Make a donation for someone lower than a joke writer?

parts.note: sub as a prefix means below, and a sub is a subordinate
a scribe is a writer; the question mark admits the joke of reading the answer as a lowly writer

explanation.surface: Giving money to support someone ranking below a comedy writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: a sub-scribe would be someone beneath a scribe.
explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe can mean to contribute money to a fund or cause, as in subscribing to a charity.

clue.text: Relative beings from an edge of space bounded by locators

indicators.note: bounded by means enclosed, so the single letter sits within the locators

parts.note: a siter is one who sites or places things, a locator

indicators.note: an edge of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Kin arrive from the rim of outer space surrounded by tracking devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters are female siblings, so they are relatives.

clue.text: Does up tip, working with sulphur

parts.note: the butt is the tip or end, as of a cigarette
on means working, as a switched-on machine
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A handyman giving a tip about working with sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: To button a coat is to fasten it, which is to do it up.

clue.text: Writer goes round stone consumer's place

indicators.note: goes round tells us the pen surrounds the weight

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: An author walks around a rock that belongs to a shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint pen. 'consumer' is one who eats.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small restaurant, a place where diners eat.

clue.text: Carbon having detrimental effect — delightful!

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
harming means having a damaging effect on something

explanation.surface: Carbon emissions damaging the planet are, ironically, praised as lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming describes something very pleasing or attractive, a direct synonym of delightful.

clue.text: Guarantee to put ageing rock star in the pen

indicators.note: in tells us the musician goes inside the pig enclosure

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
Midge Ure, the Ultravox singer from the 1980s, is a veteran rock star

explanation.surface: A promise to lock up an old rocker in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Midge Ure is a Scottish rock musician, frontman of Ultravox and co-organiser of Live Aid. 'pen' looks like prison but is a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a person or pledge that guarantees another's obligations, so it is a guarantee.

clue.text: Come another time, getting on before Chile's capital city

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a memo

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, the capital letter, of Chile

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Returning to a South American capital city at a later date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Santiago, but it is the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again, so it means come another time.

clue.text: Brummie's on the drink (cane rum), gaining weight

parts.note: Brummie is the setter, so Brummie's from the setter's view is I'm
port is a fortified wine, a classic crossword drink

indicators.note: rum, as an adjective, means odd, so the word cane is made strange by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The setter admits to drinking cane rum and putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Brummie's' gives I'M. 'rum' rearranges CANE into ANCE. 'weight' means significance, not mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight in the sense of influence or significance is importance, as in 'his opinion carries weight'.

clue.text: Jar tail off small snapper

indicators.note: tail off tells us the last letter of the word for jar is cut away

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware jar

explanation.surface: A small biting creature knocks the end off a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail off' drops the K from CROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the clipped form of crocodile, the reptile known for snapping jaws; 'small' marks the shortened word.

clue.text: Directions to king (the king of Pylos)

parts.note: N, E and S are compass directions north, east and south
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Instructions for reaching a monarch, namely the ruler of a Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer, Nestor is the aged, wise king of Pylos.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Nestor ruled Pylos and advised the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: God's very large flag

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a flag is an iris, the wild flower called yellow flag

explanation.surface: A deity's enormous banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is the plant, a type of iris, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the ancient Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife.
